page: Vultr vhf-1c-2gb is an entry-level virtual machine instance belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. The configuration utilizes a shared Intel x86_64 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, providing one virtual core mapped to a single physical core with one execution thread. The CPU architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, as well as IBRS and SSBD security mitigations. System memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB of RAM. The instance includes bundled local storage consisting of a 64 GB NVMe SSD and provides one complimentary public IPv4 address, with zero dedicated GPU accelerators present.

Benchmark results highlight an entry-tier performance profile consistent with a single shared compute core. In stress-ng testing, single-core and multi-core evaluations both registered a score of 1266.88. PassMark testing yielded an overall CPU score of 2017.05, including 1681.75 for extended instructions, 638.11 for encryption, and 258.6 for physics calculations. The memory subsystem produced a PassMark memory score of 980.81, with uncached 256 MB block reads reaching 11.09 GB/sec and writes achieving 10.16 GB/sec. Data processing tasks demonstrated average single-threaded gzip compression at 24.19 GB/sec alongside 8.48 GB/sec bzip3 decompression. At the application layer, the instance sustained 1.77 million Redis SET operations per second, a static web serving throughput of 1.68 GB/sec, and 135M parameter LLM inference rates of 172.67 prompt tokens per second and 67.18 generation tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is achieved by pairing high-speed local NVMe storage with a minimal shared compute allocation. The primary architectural tradeoff is the single shared core and modest 2.0 GB memory envelope, which limits sustained multi-threaded execution and multi-tenant resource scaling. Consequently, the instance is targeted at lightweight workloads including static web serving, low-throughput microservices, background task execution, development and testing environments, and minimal key-value caching.
description: Vultr vhf-1c-2gb is an entry-tier virtual server from the High Frequency Compute series featuring a single shared Intel x86_64 core running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. The instance comes equipped with 64 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address, operating without dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations place its compute and memory throughput within entry-level boundaries, recording 2017.05 in PassMark CPU testing and 1266.88 in stress-ng evaluations. Large-block memory transfers achieve 11.09 GB/sec read and 10.16 GB/sec write throughput. While constrained by its single-core configuration, the server achieves 1.77 million Redis SET operations per second and 24.19 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. This shared-core profile offers a cost-efficient foundation for lightweight workloads such as low-traffic web serving, development environments, background job processing, and modest caching instances.
